case_name: Bhaba Nanda Sarma and Others v State of Assam
respondent:
State of Assam
Supreme Court of India

12 October 1977
riminal Appeal No. 155 of 1972.

statutes.act: Read With Section 34 And Section 323 Read With Section 34 Of The Indian Penal Code

facts: The occurrence took place on November 10, 1967, at about 7:00 A.M. in a village near Barpeta in Assam.
Shashi-Mohan Sarma, a person who lost his life as a result of the assault on him, was proceeding to his field with some mustard seeds in a basket.
Gopi Nath Sarma, P.W.2, was going with some cattle to tether them in the field.
The three appellants, Bhaba Nanda Sarma, Phanidhar Sarma, and Harendra Nath Sarma, chased Shashi Mohan.
Shashi Mohan ran towards his brother Gopi Nath raising alarm.
Bhaba Nanda caught hold of both the hands of Shashi Mohan from behind.
Phanidhar gave him a blow on his head with the dolibari.
Harendra struck Shashi Mohan on his head and other parts of his body with the iron rod.
Shashi Mohan was taken to the hospital where he died at about 3:00 A.M. on November 11, 1967, as a result of severe injuries caused to him by Phanidhar and Harendra.
issues: Whether the conviction of all three appellants under section 302 with the aid of section 34 of the Penal Code is justified in law.
Whether Bhaba Nanda's participation in the crime was sufficient to attract the application of section 34.
petitioner_arguments: The prosecution must prove facts to justify an inference that all the participants of the act had shared a common intention to commit the criminal act which was finally committed by one or more of the participants.
Bhaba Nanda did not use his lathi for causing any injuries on Shashi.
His participation in the crime, therefore, did not take him to the extent of sharing the common intention to cause his murder.
respondent_arguments: The High Court has rightly believed the testimony of the eye witnesses.
Phanidhar and Harendra undoubtedly shared a common intention to cause such bodily injuries to Shashi Mohan which were sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause his death.
court_reasoning: In our opinion, the High Court was right in reversing the judgment of the Trial Judge and interfering with the order of acquittal.
The four reasons given by the learned Sessions Judge were of a flimsy nature.
It did not justify the entertaining of any doubt in regard to the prosecution story on the basis of these reasons.
holding: The conviction of all three appellants under section 302 with the aid of section 34 of the Penal Code is justified in law.

Bhaba Nanda can be held guilty only under section 304 Part II as he had intentionally joined in the commission of an act with the knowledge that the assault on Shashi was likely to result in his death.
